sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: h1 (notes/hooks.md). A figure that has to be built from a table's unit costs while the table prints two shortcuts beside them (its own total for another head count and a rounded yearly rate); the shape of aq-02157 q04. Target medium; hard is also open (user, 2026-10-13: no Easy slot, "target medium and high"). Quick test 2026-10-13: survived (user chat, no panel). No difficulty run yet.
- Dependency plan: D03 Table 3 gives seven lines with unit and total cost for 50 workers over three years. Total equals unit for the sponsor application (1,000 and 1,000); for the other lines total = unit × 50 (30,500, 9,950, 100,000, 40,000) or unit × 50 × 3 (150,000, 93,600). D01 Q70 gives the plant's shortfall, 150 people. Per worker: 610 + 199 + 2,000 + 800 = 3,609 once, 1,000 + 624 = 1,624 a year. 150 × 3,609 + 450 × 1,624 + 1,000 = 1,273,150.
- Universe: not a list. Every line of Table 3 is used. The table's printed total checks the reading: 1,000 + 50 × 3,609 + 150 × 1,624 = 425,050.
- Necessity: without D03 there are no unit costs (searched "£610", "£199", "£624", "Skills Charge", "Health Surcharge" in all three documents: Table 3 only; D03 para 50 also gives the Northern Ireland Pork and Bacon Forum's "about £1,200 per worker" and the BMPA's "between £5K - £10K per candidate", neither the Association's). Without D01 there is no head count: "150 people" and "1,000 people" occur once, at Q70. D03 keeps only "around 15% to 16% short on staff" (para 5), with no plant size, so the 150 cannot be rebuilt from it; the question prints neither 1,000 nor 150 for that reason. D02 holds neither input.
- Selected-lever checks: not a which-items question; no decoy required. Rounded route recomputed and different: 2,834 × 150 × 3 = 1,275,300 against 1,273,150 (425,050 / 150 = 2,833.67, which the table prints as £2,834). Pro-rata route: 3 × 425,050 = 1,275,150. Every unit cost times 150: 150 × 9,481 = 1,422,150.
- Targeted failure modes: Unit or basis / Rounding, scale or sign: Table 3 mixes a per-company line with per-worker and per-worker-per-year lines; scaling the 50-worker total by three gives 1,275,150 and the rounded rate gives 1,275,300. Both recomputed by script. Which wrong answer the easier solver gave in the quick test is not known (no panel); to be matched to the wrong answers observed after the first difficulty run, before Submit. Considered and not declared: the application charged per worker (1,422,150), which no observation supports yet.
- Calculation verification: author arithmetic, then script (2026-10-13): per worker 8,481; 50 workers 425,050 (matches the printed total); 150 workers 1,273,150; pro-rata 1,275,150; rounded rate 1,275,300; all-unit 1,422,150. Units pounds; no rounding in the gold.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: searching "Labour Providers" lands on D03 paras 50 (Table 3), 61 and 65 and on Doc 3's Q117 (an MP quoting the Association on causes, no costs). Searching "plant" in D01 gives Allen's 1,000-person example (Q70) and his members' automation examples (Q73). No passage states a cost for 150 workers. The bundle overview mentions neither the table nor the 150. Shortest route: Table 3, Q70, six operations.
- Precision/readings: (1) three times the 50-worker total, £1,275,150: rejected by "unit costs" and "one company" and by the table itself, but it is the natural shortcut because 150 is three times 50; the form's "One defensible answer" check will show whether its solvers take it. (2) The printed £2,834 a year per worker, £1,275,300: the table's own rounding. (3) The sponsor application charged for every worker, £1,422,150: the table charges it once for 50 workers. (4) "example plant" read as one of Allen's members' automation cases (Q73, an 800-people plant that "would have saved them 100 people"): those plants are not said to lack staff. (5) "the staff ... lacked" read as 15% or 16% of 1,000, giving 150 or 160: Allen states 150.
- Completeness: complete capture, no gaps (notes/intake.json). All three documents read in full. The Association's written evidence (LS0088) is not in the bundle; D03 reproduces its table, and the gold uses only what D03 prints. The Minister's remarks on these costs (14 December 2021, not in the bundle) are reported in D03 para 50 and change no figure.
- Style/set review: 25 words, one ask. q02 (a butcher's starting salary against the visa threshold) uses the same two documents and shares no input or answer path with this question.
- Warnings answered: see the hand-over note; filled in after the mechanical preflight.
sections.question: At the Association of Labour Providers' unit costs, what would one company pay to recruit, for three years, the staff Nick Allen's example plant lacked?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 1, Table 3 in the section on the cost of using the immigration system): the Association of Labour Providers costs a business recruiting workers for three years through the Skilled Worker Visa route, line by line, with a unit cost and a total for each line. For the sponsor application the total is the same as the unit cost, so a company pays it once. Every other line is charged for each worker, and two of them for each year as well.
Step 2. Source input and calculation (Doc 1, Table 3): the charges paid once for each worker are the visa at £610, the Certificate of Sponsorship at £199, recruitment at £2,000 and travel at £800: 610 + 199 + 2,000 + 800 = 3,609 pounds.
Step 3. Source input and calculation (Doc 1, Table 3): the charges paid every year for each worker are the Immigration Skills Charge at £1,000 and the Immigration Health Surcharge at £624: 1,000 + 624 = 1,624 pounds a year. The sponsor application, the one line a company pays once, is a further £1,000.
Step 4. Source input (Doc 2, Nick Allen of the British Meat Processors Association, in his first answer to the Chair): he takes a meat plant as his example and says that on any morning it is "150 people short".
Step 5. Calculation (Doc 1 and Doc 2): worker-years for those staff over the table's three years: 150 × 3 = 450.
Step 6. Calculation (Doc 1 and Doc 2): once-only charges for all of them: 150 × 3,609 = 541,350 pounds.
Step 7. Calculation (Doc 1 and Doc 2): yearly charges over the three years: 450 × 1,624 = 730,800 pounds.
Step 8. Calculation (Doc 1 and Doc 2): with the one sponsor application added: 541,350 + 730,800 + 1,000 = 1,273,150 pounds.
Step 9. Shortcuts that miss (Doc 1 and Doc 2): the plant's shortfall is three times the head count the table was built for, but tripling the table's own total would charge the sponsor application three times. The table's rounded yearly figure per worker overstates the cost as well. Pricing each line at its unit cost gives neither result.
Step 10. Final answer (Doc 1 and Doc 2): one company would pay £1,273,150.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Unit or basis
How a careless solver fails: Rounding, scale or sign

Why these are traps: Unit or basis: Doc 1's Table 3 charges the sponsor application once per company and every other line per worker. Tripling its £425,050 total for Doc 2's 150 workers gives £1,275,150, and its rounded £2,834 yearly rate gives £1,275,300. Priced line by line, the cost is £1,273,150.
